## The estimand statement {#the-estimand-statement}

::: {.claimcard}
"The expected change in [unit quantity] among [target population] for a 1-percentage-point difference in unemployment, holding [assumptions] fixed."
:::

::: {.small}
- Unit quantity – the framing of a *person*, or the mean of a *country-year*?
- Target population – which countries, which years?
- Assumptions – what is held fixed, and so which comparison is made?
:::

::: {.fragment}
**In the chat, now:** your one-sentence estimand statement for the claim. Type it, hold it, send on "go".
:::

::: notes
Back to our own paper, with the template of Lundberg and colleagues in hand, and this one is a chat exercise. Fill the brackets for the claim on the card: whose framing, which population of countries and years, and what you hold fixed while unemployment changes. Type your sentence, hold it, and send it when I say go. [go; read three or four aloud.] Look at the spread. Some of you wrote about a person, some about a country-year, some held the year fixed and some did not. None of these is wrong. They are different questions, and the coefficient means something different in each. Keep your sentence, because the five analysts made exactly this kind of choice, and the next slide shows which questions they ended up answering.
:::

## The five Task 2 analyses {#the-five-task-2-analyses .smaller}

::: {.small}
| Analyst | Unit | Outcome | Unemployment | Comparison | Recorded |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| KQXUE | 270 country-years | share | Eurostat, 20–64, % of population | country FE | t = −7.17 |
| C6HJR | 270 country-years | share | World Bank | country and year FE | t = −3.80 |
| KEVF1 | 209,826 respondents | count of five items | Eurostat, mostly from 2009 | random intercepts | t = −5.90 |
| PRL47 | 394,575 respondents | share, silent left out | Eurostat, quarterly, 25–64 | three levels, controls | z = −3.59 |
| 018OL | 420 country-wave cells | mean of five items | Eurostat, 15–74 | random intercepts | t = −1.21 |

::: {.fragment .small}
The instructions fixed the outcome and the predictor, and the five analysts still answered five different questions. Three of them worked on means of countries or of cells, and those three are the reproductions of Part 3.
:::

::: notes
Here are the five analyses of the second task, the one with instructions, as each analyst actually ran it. Read the table across rather than down. The units differ: two analysts worked on country-years, one on cells of a country in one wave, two on several hundred thousand respondents. The outcome differs: a share of mentions, a count, a mean. Each took a different unemployment series, and each made a different comparison, within a country, within a country and a year, or through random intercepts. [advance] So the instructions fixed the outcome and the predictor, and still produced five estimand statements. Three of the five work on means of countries or of cells, which can be published, and those are the three that you can choose between in Part 3.
:::
